key_insight: MemSkill replaces rigid, hand-designed memory operations with learnable, evolvable "memory skills"—structured, reusable routines for extracting, consolidating, and pruning memory—so agents can adapt memory behavior to diverse interactions and long histories.
problem_solved: Current LLM agent memory systems use a small set of static procedures that hard-code human priors, making them inflexible across interaction patterns and inefficient when scaling to long conversation histories.
method: Reframe extraction, consolidation, and pruning as parameterized memory skills that can be learned rather than hand-crafted.
Organize skills as structured, reusable routines that can be applied across contexts and updated from interaction data.
Introduce a self-evolution mechanism that adapts and refines the skill library over time so agents improve memory handling without manual redesign.
impact: MemSkill enables more flexible, scalable, and efficient memory management for LLM agents, improving long-term coherence and reducing manual engineering of memory operations—beneficial for deployed conversational and multi-step AI systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed hand-designed ops (rigid flow) vs. MemSkill pipeline (learnable skills, adaptable flow)
Skill library schematic: icons for Extract / Consolidate / Prune with arrows showing reuse across tasks
Evolution loop: interactions → skill evaluation → adaptation/update (self-evolving agents)
Performance chart: memory efficiency or task performance over long histories comparing baseline vs. MemSkill
paper_title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Tao Feng, Weizhi Zhang
